visual_goal: Show the four gates in order: supply first, data rights second, judgement and liability third, and cost only for the remaining commodity choices.
prompt: A top-to-bottom decision flow. At the top, a rounded tile labeled 'Capability'. Below it, four orange diamond gates stacked vertically and joined by single downward arrows, labeled from top to bottom: 'Supply', 'Data rights', 'Liability', 'Cost curve'. Each of the first three gates has one side exit to the right: from 'Supply', one arrow to a teal tile labeled 'License or partner'; from 'Data rights', one arrow labeled 'no' to a red tile labeled 'Renegotiate or reject'; from 'Liability', one arrow labeled 'yes' to a blue tile with a small shield icon labeled 'Own the logic'. From 'Cost curve' at the bottom, two arrows: one down-left to a green tile labeled 'Buy or partner' and one down-right to a blue tile labeled 'Build or adopt'. These twelve labels are the only words in the image.
alt: A capability passes four gates in order (supply, data rights, liability, cost curve); side exits lead to license or partner, renegotiate or reject, and own the logic, and the cost gate splits into buy or partner versus build or adopt.

visual_goal: Show what Axleby owns (products, canonical services, Charter, the budget broker) and what it rents (licensed data, bought services, partners) behind adapters.
prompt: A left-to-right architecture illustration split by a vertical dashed boundary line in the right third. Left of the boundary, owned components in blue: a stack of app windows labeled 'Products'; one arrow from 'Products' to a large central block labeled 'Canonical services'; directly above 'Canonical services', a small plain shield with a check mark, labeled 'Charter' underneath joined to it by one short plain line; one arrow from 'Canonical services' to a gate-shaped tile labeled 'Budget broker'; one arrow from 'Budget broker' to a plug-shaped tile labeled 'Supplier adapters'; lower down, one arrow from 'Canonical services' to a second plug-shaped tile labeled 'Hitch'. Right of the boundary, rented components in orange, in three rows: top a database stack labeled 'Licensed data', middle a gear box labeled 'Bought services', bottom a handshake tile labeled 'Partners', level with 'Hitch'. 'Supplier adapters' has exactly two outgoing arrows: one to 'Licensed data' and one to 'Bought services'. 'Hitch' has exactly one outgoing arrow, straight right to 'Partners'. 'Products' has exactly one arrow, into 'Canonical services'. Each of these nine labels appears exactly once, written once below its own icon; no letters inside icons.
alt: Products talk to canonical services, which consult Charter and pass paid calls through the budget broker to supplier adapters for licensed data and bought services, and through Hitch to partners.
